answer: An agent economy can make reputation portable only when each identity posts a refundable stake in a vault and signs every job claim with a key bound to that stake. If an agent is caught double-claiming or failing a task, a verifier publishes the signed evidence; a contract checks it and slashes the deposit. Creating many sybils then means locking real capital in each account, not merely minting names, and keeping those stakes tied up through every voyage. A cipher can protect private task details, but it cannot hide the signed proof needed for slashing.
